record.final_answer:
No. The report doesn't answer the TLS question at all — and its plain-TCP number wouldn't transfer to us even if it did.

What the report actually says (Marrowlog 2.4 perf report, 2026 Q2, published 2026-06-18):

- Result: one agent shipped 180,000 lines/s to a collector on 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, CPU at 85%.
- Method: plain TCP output — "TLS was not enabled in any run"; disk buffer off; batch_lines 500; input lines 200 bytes or shorter; median of three 30-minute runs.
- Not covered: TLS to the collector, lines longer than 200 bytes, and the disk buffer. TLS is planned for the Q4 report.

Why it can't be extrapolated to our peak (/stand/ws/README.md: 50,000 lines/s per agent, ~900 bytes/line, 1 vCPU reserved):

- Bytes, not lines, are the load here. Our peak is 50,000 × 900 B = 45 MB/s. The benchmark's ceiling is 180,000 × 200 B = 36 MB/s — and only at 85% CPU on unencrypted TCP. We'd need 1.25x that byte rate.
- Our lines are 4.5x longer than anything they measured. At their byte ceiling we'd be at ~40,000 lines/s, below our 50,000 peak. (The 180,000-line figure looks like 2.8x headroom only if you compare lines; that comparison is invalid.)
- TLS is additional CPU on the same 1 vCPU, and it's precisely what was excluded. There's no published figure for its cost.

So: not demonstrated. The honest statement to Security is that the vendor report shows no TLS measurement and our byte rate already exceeds their plain-TCP ceiling, so capacity under TLS is unverified. The batch_lines 500 and disk-buffer-off settings do match our config/agent.yaml, which helps the comparison but doesn't close either gap.

To get a real answer, measure it: run one agent at 50,000 lines/s of realistic 900-byte lines into a collector with TLS on, on 1 vCPU, and watch CPU and drop rate. Also worth asking Marrowlog for the Q4 TLS numbers or an early internal figure before committing to the end-of-quarter deadline — if TLS costs ~15-20% CPU on an already 85%-utilised profile, the current sizing is likely short and would need either more vCPU per sidecar or line trimming (stack traces are the bulk of those 900 bytes).
